entries.title: fix: convert SecurityHeadersMiddleware to pure ASGI
entries.body:
SecurityHeadersMiddleware was the last middleware in the stack still subclassing BaseHTTPMiddleware, after CommitSession, AuthToken, WebsocketUpgradeGuard and Redirect were all moved to pure ASGI in utils/asgi_middleware.py. BaseHTTPMiddleware re-buffers the response body through an anyio task group, which has known issues with streaming and Content-Length-bearing responses (e.g. the FileResponse returned by /api/v1/audio/speech).

Reimplement it as a pure-ASGI middleware that stamps the configured security headers onto the http.response.start message via MutableHeaders and forwards all body chunks untouched, matching the pattern already used by its four siblings. set_security_headers() and all its helpers are unchanged.

entries.title: fix: restore prompt confirmation for sandboxed tool result embeds
entries.body:
Tool result embeds are rendered by FullHeightIframe as srcdoc iframes without allow-same-origin by default, so their postMessage events carry the opaque origin "null". The trust gate in Chat.svelte's onMessageHandler only accepted same-origin sources or the global iframeSandboxAllowSameOrigin opt-in, so input:prompt, input:prompt:submit and action:submit from Open WebUI's own embeds were silently dropped before reaching the "Confirm Prompt from Embed" dialog that exists for exactly this cross-origin case. The documented Rich UI flow (confirmation dialog on submit, no same-origin access required) was unreachable either way: with the setting off the message was dropped, and with it on the embed became same-origin and submitted immediately without confirmation.

FullHeightIframe now registers its iframes' contentWindow in a module-level set and Chat.svelte additionally trusts a prompt message when event.source is in that set. Window identity cannot be forged: windows of external pages embedding or opening Open WebUI are never in the set, so they remain blocked exactly as before, and prompt submission from own embeds still requires the user to accept the existing confirmation dialog.

Fixes #26912

entries.title: fix: socket reconnect recovery never runs for chats started from the home page
entries.body:
When a chat is started from the home page, the URL is switched to /c/{id} with history.replaceState, so the Chat component is never remounted and chatIdProp stays empty for the lifetime of that view. Both websocket recovery paths, handleSocketConnect and the chat:active fallback, are gated on chatIdProp and therefore never run for these chats. After any websocket drop during a response (mobile backgrounding, VPN or IP change, wake from sleep) the completed response is never fetched and the chat stays stuck in a loading state until a manual page refresh. Chats opened directly via /c/{id} recover fine, which is why the bug only reproduces reliably on freshly started chats.

Gate both recovery paths on the chatId store instead, which is set for every persisted chat, and let loadChat fall back to it so the recovery reload also works when chatIdProp is empty. Chats opened via /c/{id} behave exactly as before and temporary chats stay excluded.

The same gate likely explains the remaining reports in #26315.

Fixes #26844

entries.title: fix: Milvus multitenancy scalar index creation on Milvus Lite
entries.body:
Enabling ENABLE_MILVUS_MULTITENANCY_MODE with the default MILVUS_URI (embedded Milvus Lite at DATA_DIR/vector_db/milvus.db) fails on the first embedding write: _create_shared_collection calls collection.create_index(RESOURCE_ID_FIELD) with no index params. A Milvus server auto-selects a scalar index type in that case, but Milvus Lite rejects the call with "create_index missing required 'index_type' parameter", so shared collection creation raises and every embedding write 500s (memory add, file upload, knowledge writes).

Keep the parameterless call as the first attempt so behavior on Milvus servers is unchanged, fall back to an explicit INVERTED scalar index, and if that also fails log a warning and continue. The scalar index only accelerates resource_id filters; inserts and filtered queries work without it, so a missing index must not break collection creation.

Verified against embedded Milvus Lite: shared collections now create (with the warning), and memory add, file upload and memory query succeed end to end. Against a Milvus server the first attempt is identical to the current code, so nothing changes where it works today.

entries.title: fix: gate allow-same-origin on the terminal file-preview iframe to prevent same-origin XSS
entries.body:
The system-terminal HTML file preview (FilePreview.svelte, serveUrl branch) rendered served HTML in an iframe that hardcoded allow-same-origin. The terminal proxy serves the file root-relative (same origin as the app) and injects no CSP, and there is no default global CSP, so script in a previewed HTML file executed in the application's own origin and could read localStorage (the session token), enabling account takeover and, for admin or workspace.functions victims, server-side RCE via Functions. The sibling srcdoc branch already gates allow-same-origin behind the iframeSandboxAllowSameOrigin setting (off by default) and injects a CSP; the serveUrl branch never received that defense. Gate allow-same-origin on the serveUrl branch identically, so by default the preview runs at an opaque origin and its scripts cannot reach the parent context. Legitimate HTML preview rendering is unaffected.

entries.title: fix: don't mutate caller's payload when resolving a pipe base model
entries.body:
generate_function_chat_completion rewrote form_data['model'] to the base model id in place. Because that dict is the same object process_chat_response later re-submits for the post-tool-call continuation, the continuation was access-checked against the base model instead of the user-facing preset. For a public preset over a private/unregistered pipe base, a non-admin's first message succeeded but the continuation after a native tool call was denied and silently swallowed, aborting the response (admins skip the user-only check, so they were unaffected).

Operate on a shallow copy of form_data, mirroring the openai/ollama routers which already substitute the base model on a copy. The continuation now re-checks the preset the user actually has access to.

### Description

Hotfix for #25771 — dragging pinned notes from the sidebar into the chat area was silently failing. The notes would not attach as context references despite the feature being implemented in #25771.

**Problem:** Dragging a pinned note from the sidebar into the chat area did nothing — no drop overlay appeared and the note was not added as a context reference.

**Root Cause (two issues):**

1. **SortableJS data conflict:** The note drag data was set via a native `on:dragstart` handler, but the notes are children of a SortableJS container. Without a custom `setData` callback, SortableJS's default behavior overwrites `text/plain` with the element's raw text content (e.g. `"Open WebUI ..."`) instead of the expected JSON (`{"type":"note","id":"..."}`). entries.title: ci: add non-blocking flaky test report job with 30-day retention
entries.body:
## Why

Playwright retries (`--retries=3`) keep CI green when a test fails and passes on retry — but that failed→passed pattern is exactly what identifies a flaky test, and today it is never captured: blob reports are deleted after 1 day, and the existing `merge-reports` job only runs when CI is red (flaky runs end green, so they are always skipped). Recent runs show the impact: wall-clock ranges from ~2 to ~47 min across runs, driven by retry variance rather than test weight.

## What

Adds a `flaky-report` job that reuses the existing merge logic but stays fully isolated from it:

- Runs on every run that executed the Playwright shards (green included) — the existing `merge-reports` HTML job is untouched.
- Merges the run's blob reports into a single JSON (`merge-reports --reporter json`), which records, per test attempt: status, error message, failure location (file:line) and the step where it stopped.
- Uploads it as a small `flaky-report` artifact (a few MB) with 30-day retention, so flakiness can be ranked over time instead of guessed from single runs.

## Design notes

- `continue-on-error: true` — metrics-only job; it can never turn CI red or block a PR.
- Playwright pinned to `1.60.0` (repo version): blob format is version-sensitive and bare `npx playwright` would fetch latest.
- Skipped when the shards didn't run (path-filtered runs have no blobs to download).
- Artifact name includes `run_attempt`, mirroring the existing `html-report` artifact, so manual re-runs don't overwrite each other.
- No test code changes; heavy blob artifacts keep their 1-day retention.

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * Added a new test-report artifact generated after test runs, making flaky test results easier to review.
  * Consolidated per-shard reports into a single JSON file for simpler inspection.
* **Chores**

  * Configured the report artifact to be retained for 30 days and named per run attempt.

entries.title: fix(docker): give runtime user a writable npm cache so stdio MCP servers start
entries.body:
## Problem

The nightly / published images (`langflowai/langflow-nightly`, `langflowai/langflow`) are built from a `registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/python-314-minimal` base, which sets `HOME=/opt/app-root/src`. In `docker/build_and_push.Dockerfile` the runtime stage runs `npm install -g npm@latest` **as root**, which seeds a **root-owned** npm cache at `/opt/app-root/src/.npm`.

At runtime the backend spawns stdio MCP servers via `npx` as the runtime user (uid 1000). npm resolves its cache to `$HOME/.npm/_cacache` = `/opt/app-root/src/.npm/_cacache` (root-owned) and fails:

```
npm error code EACCES
npm error path /opt/app-root/src/.npm/_cacache/tmp/...
npm error Your cache folder contains root-owned files ...
npm error   sudo chown -R 1000:0 "/opt/app-root/src/.npm"
```

So every stdio MCP server registers successfully but **never lists tools** — `toolsCount` stays `null` indefinitely in `GET /api/v2/mcp/servers?action_count=true`, and the UI shows *"Error loading server: Connection closed"*. The confirmed manual workaround is exactly `docker exec -u 0 <container> chown -R 1000:0 /opt/app-root/src/.npm`.

This regressed with the move to the ubi10 base (#13893), which introduced the `/opt/app-root/src` home path.

## Fix

Give the runtime user (uid 1000) a guaranteed-writable npm cache in all three runtime images that ship Node:

- Set `ENV NPM_CONFIG_CACHE=/app/.npm` — a uid-1000-owned directory, **immune to the base image's `HOME`** so a future base change can't reintroduce the bug.
- `chown -R 1000:0` + `chmod -R g+rwX` both `/app/.npm` and the default `/opt/app-root/src/.npm`, mirroring the existing `/app/langflow` ownership block and preserving OpenShift arbitrary-uid (gid 0) compatibility.

Applied to `build_and_push.Dockerfile` (the broken nightly/main image), and defensively to `build_and_push_with_extras.Dockerfile` and `build_and_push_base.Dockerfile`, which ship Node under the same ubi10 `HOME` and would hit the same class of `npx` `EACCES`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `docker build -f docker/build_and_push.Dockerfile -t lf-npm-test .`
- [ ] `docker run --rm lf-npm-test id` → `uid=1000 gid=0`
- [ ] `docker run --rm lf-npm-test ls -lan /app/.npm /opt/app-root/src/.npm` → owned by `1000:0`
- [ ] As the default user: `docker run --rm lf-npm-test npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything --help` succeeds (before: `EACCES` on `/opt/app-root/src/.npm/_cacache`)
- [ ] End-to-end: register a stdio MCP server (e.g. `npx @modelcontextprotocol/server-everything`) in a fresh container and confirm `toolsCount` is populated (non-null) and tools load

  * Added writable cache directories for the non-root runtime user, reducing `EACCES` failures during `npx` and other tooling runs.
  * Updated image permissions and cache configuration to support smoother startup in environments using npm-installed utilities.

entries.title: merge: sync release-1.11.0 into cz/hitl-v2
entries.body:
Hey @Cristhianzl, the v2 workflow router seam just landed on release-1.11.0 (#13816), and it rewrote `api/v2/workflow.py` pretty heavily. Your branch was about a month behind release, so merging up was going to be painful. I did the merge for you here so you can just merge this into `cz/hitl-v2` instead of resolving it yourself.

47 files conflicted. The rule I followed everywhere: take release's structure and hygiene, keep your durable + HITL semantics on top. I tried hard not to drop anything of yours, but you know the HITL intent better than I do, so please look closely at the files below.

## What I had to make a call on

**`api/v2/workflow.py`** is the big one. Release moved the POST run path into lfx (`create_workflow_router` bound to `LangflowWorkflowHost`) and split helpers into `workflow_execution.py`. So this file is now release's seam skeleton (`resolve_flow_for_execution`, `authorize_flow_action`, `run_sync_with_mapping`, `build_stream_response`) with your durable route bodies dropped into it: status reconstruct with the `Job.result` fallback, the stop signal-before-CANCELLED ordering, `service.events` replay, and your `/pending` + `/{job_id}/resume` routes. Background submit goes through your durable facade, not release's process-local `_BACKGROUND_RUNS` buffer.

**`workflow_execution.py`** keeps release's newer body (the `asyncio.wait_for` execution ceiling, `_WorkflowEventQueue` overflow adapter, `terminal_error_seen` dedup) and gains your `job_id` / `resume` params plus the `human_input_required` frame-type mapping so the durable runner still detects the pause. I did not port your `event_manager.on_error` call in `drive()`, because release deliberately replaced it with the consumer-side guaranteed fallback. I think that's right, but flag me if you disagree.

**`build.py`** unions your pause plumbing with release's `run_id`-keyed vertex-build persistence.

## Three things I fixed that weren't strictly conflicts

- `idempotency_key` never reached the service. `ParsedWorkflowRun` didn't carry the field, so `parse_workflow_run_request` dropped it and your dedupe + `DuplicateJobError` -> 409 was dead through the seam. Added it to the dataclass and threaded it through `submit_background_with_mapping`.
- Durable runs now pass `run_id=str(job_id)` into the build loop so vertex builds are keyed by the durable job_id. Without it `reconstruct_workflow_response_from_job_id` found nothing, fell back to the `Job.result` rebuild, and a completed job's status reported `session_id: null`. `track_job_status=False` still holds, so no duplicate WORKFLOW row.
- The auto-merge silently dropped `HumanInputContent` from both `ContentType` unions (the class survived, the `Tag("human_input")` arm didn't). Restored in lfx and langflow-base.

Also re-parented your migration chain onto release's head (`c3e7a1b9d2f4`), so there's a single alembic head again. And `graph/base.py` needed care: release rewrote `exclude_branches_conditionally`, and taking release's file wholesale silently deleted `check_and_handle_pause` / `request_pause` / `build_checkpoint` / `resume_from_checkpoint`. Kept both.

## Tests

- `test_workflow.py` 28/28, `test_workflow_agui.py` 70/70, `test_workflow_public.py` + `test_mcp_utils.py` green
- lfx: `tests/unit/workflow` 224, `tests/unit/graph` 275, serve suites green

Two follow-ups I left alone: `api/v2/workflow_background.py` (release's process-local buffer) is now production-dead since your durable substrate replaced it, though some tests still exercise it directly. And `test_workflow_agui.py` had no HITL-specific tests on either side, so if yours live elsewhere nothing was lost, but worth a check.

## You pushed while I was merging

I pulled in `durable HITL background on lfx serve` and `code review improvements` too, so this is current with your branch tip.

Your `LFX_SERVE_DURABLE_DB` mount in `serve_app.py` kept its shape: the stateless `else` still returns the seam's `create_workflow_router(ServeWorkflowHost(...))`. Worth knowing, since it landed after the seam did: `ServeWorkflowHost.resolve_caller` now resolves the verified identity and `_run_user_id` threads it into the run, so `DurableServeWorkflowHost` inherits serve v2 identity for the sync and stream paths. Your `submit_background` override doesn't thread it, which may be fine for background, but you'd know better than me.

Your ownership tightening in `get_workflow_status` auto-merged into the durable body. `test_serve_durable.py` is 9/9.

entries.title: feat(mcp): persist MCP servers in a database table
entries.body:
Fixes #13970

## Problem

MCP servers are stored per-user as a JSON file (`_mcp_servers_<user_id>.json`) written through the files API, and edits are serialized only by an in-process `asyncio.Lock` (`api/v2/mcp.py`). With more than one Uvicorn worker or replica that lock doesn't coordinate, so concurrent edits do a non-atomic read-modify-write of the whole file and the last write wins — servers are silently dropped. With local-disk storage each replica also keeps its own copy, so the list diverges per replica. Net: MCP config is unsafe above one worker/replica.

## Solution

Store MCP servers in a new `mcp_server` table — one row per server, unique on `(user_id, name)`:

- `get_server_list` / `get_server` / `update_server` become per-row reads/upserts, and the in-process `_update_server_locks` is removed. Concurrent edits to *different* servers touch *different* rows and never contend; a same-name race is caught by the unique constraint and folded into an update. Correct at any worker/replica count, with no in-process lock.
- Secret values (`env` / `headers`) are encrypted at rest with the existing Fernet key (they were plaintext on disk) and decrypted on read.
- Alembic migration `247308ce2598` (Expand phase) creates the table.
- **Backwards compatible:** the REST shape (`{"mcpServers": {...}}`) and all function signatures are unchanged. Existing `_mcp_servers_*.json` files are imported by an idempotent, multi-replica-safe startup backfill (`api/utils/mcp/backfill.py`) plus a `langflow migrate-mcp [--dry-run]` CLI; the legacy file is left in place so a rollback is safe. The `is_mcp_servers_locked` RBAC gate and the PATCH `merge_existing` semantics are preserved.

### Blast radius

The rewritten functions are consumed by the v2 REST endpoints, `api/utils/mcp/config_utils.py`, `agentic_mcp.py`, `api/v1/projects_mcp_helpers.py`, and the lfx MCP component (`get_server`). All keep working because the signatures and `{"mcpServers": {...}}` output are unchanged. The pre-DB file reader is preserved as `_read_legacy_mcp_file` (used only by the backfill); the files-API upload path is untouched.

## Testing

- New `tests/unit/api/v2/test_mcp_db_store.py`: concurrency (distinct-server adds all survive; same-name race → one row), CRUD round-trip, secrets encrypted-at-rest / decrypted-on-read, and the file→table backfill.
- `tests/unit/api/v2/test_mcp_servers_file.py`: the concurrent lost-update regression test now runs against the real DB store.
- Model/migration consistency passes on SQLite **and** Postgres 16 (migration applies + downgrades on the `release-1.11.0` head); ruff and the migration Expand-phase check are green.
- Additionally validated by driving the running app (v2 API + the "Add MCP Server" UI) and a 4-process shared-DB run (40/40 concurrent adds survive).


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **New Features**
  * MCP server settings are now stored in the database instead of per-user files.
  * Added a migration command to import existing MCP configurations, with a dry-run option.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Improved handling of concurrent MCP updates to avoid lost changes.
  * Preserved existing server entries during simultaneous saves.
  * Added safer startup migration that continues even if legacy data import fails.

* **Security**
  * Sensitive MCP configuration values are now encrypted at rest and decrypted on read.

entries.title: fix: prevent LangfuseResourceManager deepcopy failure in Agent/Tool Calling Agent
entries.body:
## Summary

Fixes #13965

**Symptom:** Using the Agent or Tool Calling Agent (LangChain) component with Langfuse tracing enabled fails with:
```
LangfuseResourceManager.new() missing 3 required keyword-only arguments: 'public_key', 'secret_key', and 'base_url'
```

**Root cause:** The #13429 fix (c4d27818a) introduced `_RootRunReparentingCallbackHandler` as a `CallbackHandler` subclass. `CallbackHandler` internally holds a `LangfuseResourceManager`. When a component (e.g. ChromaDB tool) is `deepcopy`'d at invocation time by `component_tool.py` (to prevent race conditions — issue #8791), Python calls `LangfuseResourceManager.__new__()` with no arguments during copy construction. Newer langfuse builds changed `__new__` to require explicit credentials, so this raises a `TypeError`.

**Fix:** Add `__deepcopy__` to `_RootRunReparentingCallbackHandler` to return `self` instead of attempting a structural copy. The handler holds no per-invocation mutable state, so sharing one instance across concurrent tool copies is safe.

This is the same root cause and same class of fix already documented in `flow_loader.py` for the agentic path (issue #13429 comment: *"Any later deepcopy/pickle of those tools triggers `LangfuseResourceManager.__new__()` with no kwargs and raises"*).

## Changes

- `src/backend/base/langflow/services/tracing/langfuse.py` — add `__deepcopy__` to `_RootRunReparentingCallbackHandler` (12 lines added)

## Testing

Verified with a standalone simulation that reproduces the exact `LangfuseResourceManager.__new__()` failure and confirms the fix prevents it:
```
PASS: deepcopy returns self, no LangfuseResourceManager.__new__() error
CONFIRMED BUG EXISTS without fix: LangfuseResourceManager.__new__() missing 3 required keyword-only arguments
```

Existing `test_langfuse_orphan_generation.py` and `test_langfuse_v3_compatibility.py` are unaffected (the fix does not change any callback dispatch logic).

  * Improved stability when copying shared tracing handlers, preventing failures in workflows that reuse the same handler across multiple calls.

entries.title: fix: cascade span deletes when clearing traces for a flow
entries.body:
## Summary

Fixes #13955, where clicking "Clear all" on a flow's traces silently fails. The actual database error (visible in Postgres logs) is:

```
ERROR:  update or delete on table "trace" violates foreign key constraint "span_trace_id_fkey" on table "span"
DETAIL:  Key (id)=(...) is still referenced from table "span".
STATEMENT:  DELETE FROM trace WHERE trace.flow_id = $1
```

### Root cause

`delete_traces_by_flow` (`api/v1/traces.py`) deletes traces for a flow with a single bulk statement for efficiency:

```python
delete_stmt = sa.delete(TraceTable).where(col(TraceTable.flow_id) == flow_id)
await session.execute(delete_stmt)
```

`TraceTable.spans` declares `cascade="all, delete-orphan"`, but that is an ORM-level relationship cascade — it only runs when SQLAlchemy loads and deletes objects through the unit of work (e.g. `session.delete(trace)`). A raw bulk `DELETE` statement never goes through the ORM cascade machinery, so it relies entirely on the database's own foreign key behavior.

Looking at the schema, `trace.flow_id -> flow.id` was created with `ondelete="CASCADE"`, but `span.trace_id -> trace.id` was not (see the original migration `3478f0bd6ccb_add_trace_and_span_tables.py`). So the database has no instruction to cascade the delete to `span` rows, and Postgres correctly rejects the delete to protect referential integrity.

This isn't limited to "Clear all" either — any bulk-style delete of trace rows (not just this one endpoint) would hit the same wall, since the fix belongs at the schema level rather than in a specific call site.

### Fix

- `SpanTable.trace_id` now declares `ondelete="CASCADE"` on its `Field`, matching the pattern already used by `TraceBase.flow_id`.
- A new Alembic migration (`e1705947c729`) brings existing databases (SQLite and PostgreSQL) in line with the updated model, following the same defensive pattern as the existing `59a272d6669a_ensure_trace_flow_id_cascade` migration (which fixed the analogous `trace.flow_id` FK back in #12002). It looks up the live foreign key on `span.trace_id`, drops it, and recreates it with `ON DELETE CASCADE` — a no-op if a database is already correct. On SQLite, where reflected anonymous constraints report no name, it supplies a `naming_convention` to `batch_alter_table` so the existing constraint can still be located and replaced (verified manually; a fresh migration chain otherwise leaves a duplicate, un-cascaded constraint behind).

No application code changes were needed — with the constraint fixed at the database level, the existing bulk-delete statement in `delete_traces_by_flow` now cascades correctly on its own, and the same fix also covers any other path that might bulk-delete traces in the future.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `test_span_cascade_delete.py`: seeds a flow/trace/span through a real (non-mocked) FK-enforcing SQLite engine, then issues the exact same bulk `DELETE FROM trace WHERE flow_id = ...` statement `delete_traces_by_flow` uses, and asserts it succeeds and the span is cascade-deleted. Confirmed this test fails with `IntegrityError: FOREIGN KEY constraint failed` (matching the issue's Postgres error) when the model fix is reverted, and passes with it applied.
- [x] Verified the migration directly: ran the full migration chain against a fresh scratch SQLite database, confirmed a single `ON DELETE CASCADE` constraint results (no duplicates), that `downgrade` reverts it cleanly, and that re-running `upgrade` on an already-fixed database is a no-op.
- [x] `408 passed, 3 skipped` on the full traces/tracing suite: `test_traces_api.py`, `services/database/models/traces/`, `services/tracing/`.
- [x] `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on all changed files.

entries.title: feat(a2a): implement tasks/cancel with a durable terminal state
entries.body:
tasks/cancel was unimplemented (the executor's cancel raised NotImplementedError). Two things made the naive fix wrong, both caught by tests:

- The SDK's V2 request handler only preempts a *live* producer. A parked input-required task has already finished its producer, so the SDK's `on_cancel_task` no-ops and returns the task unchanged.
- A live run whose event queue closes as its producer is cancelled can drop the CANCELED event, leaving the task stuck `working`.

So a `_DurableCancelHandler` overrides `on_cancel_task`: it delegates (still preempts a live producer on the same worker), then forces a terminal CANCELED into the durable store and the returned task, covering both cases. `DurableTaskStore.save` also won't let a run that completes after the cancel clobber a terminal CANCELED. `executor.cancel` is now just the stream cancel event (it must not raise, or the SDK marks the task failed).

Cross-worker preemption of a running flow is out of scope: the producer registry and queues are per-process, so a cancel on another worker marks the store CANCELED but can't stop the other worker's run. That needs the shared cancel signal from the async/durable execution path.

Tests: a parked input-required task is canceled end-to-end and reads back canceled from the store, and the store won't overwrite a terminal CANCELED with a later completion.

entries.title: feat(a2a): add an owner-scoped agent registry endpoint
entries.body:
Discovery today is one card per flow URL: an orchestrator has to know each flow id up front. This adds `GET /api/v1/a2a/agents`, which lists the caller's own A2A-published agent flows (agent-typed + a2a_enabled), each with its agent-card URL, so agents can be enumerated.

Auth model: authenticated and owner-scoped, mirroring the MCP-projects catalog. A public cross-user directory would strip the per-flow card's unguessable-id obscurity and expose every user's agents, so the registry lists only the calling user's agents. The per-flow card itself stays public (unchanged), it's just no longer the only way to find an agent.

Test: the listing returns only the caller's agent + a2a_enabled flows (a disabled flow, a non-agent flow, and another user's agent are all excluded) with the correct card URL.

entries.title: feat(a2a): set the card protocolVersion explicitly instead of the sdk default
entries.body:
The agent card advertised its protocolVersion via the a2a-sdk compat default, so an sdk bump could silently change what we advertise. This pins it to an explicit `A2A_PROTOCOL_VERSION` constant that the card reads.

The value stays 0.3.0 on purpose: the server speaks the JSON-RPC v0.3 surface via `JsonRpcDispatcher(enable_v0_3_compat=True)`, so 0.3.0 is the truthful protocol version. The latest spec is on the 1.x line, but we don't serve that yet, and advertising 1.x while speaking 0.3 would be worse than a stale-but-honest version. When the server moves onto the 1.x protocol, bump the constant.

`preferredTransport` (JSONRPC) is already correct, so it's untouched.

Test: the served card's protocolVersion is asserted to equal the constant and 0.3.0, so a future bump has to update both deliberately.

entries.title: Support MiniMax M3 chat model
entries.body:
## Summary

Add support for [MiniMax M3](https://platform.minimax.io/docs/api-reference/text-openai-api) as a chat model. M3 is served over an OpenAI-compatible API, so it already works through Khoj's existing OpenAI provider path (an `AiModelApi` with `model-type: OpenAI` and the MiniMax API base URL). This PR adds the two small bits of model-specific handling Khoj uses for other third-party OpenAI-compatible models.

MiniMax M2 is already recognized as an in-stream thinking model in `is_instream_thinking_model`; this extends the same handling to M3.

## Changes

- **In-stream thinking detection**: MiniMax M3, like M2 and Kimi K2 Thinking, emits its reasoning inline as `<think>...</think>` blocks in the content stream. Add `MiniMax-m3` to `is_instream_thinking_model` so its reasoning is parsed by the in-stream thought processor instead of leaking into the visible chat response.
- **Cost tracking**: register `MiniMax-M3` pay-as-you-go pricing in `model_to_cost` (`$0.6` input / `$2.4` output / `$0.12` cache read per M tokens).
- **Tests**: add unit tests for in-stream thinking detection and the M3 cost entry.

## How to use

Create an AI Model API with the MiniMax base URL (`https://api.minimax.io/v1`) and your `MINIMAX_API_KEY`, then add a chat model named `MiniMax-M3` with `model-type` set to `OpenAI`.

## Testing

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files
- Added unit tests in `tests/test_openai_utils.py` covering in-stream thinking detection (M2/M3/Kimi true; gpt-4o/claude/gemini false) and the M3 cost lookup
- Verified `MiniMax-M3` is a valid model id via the MiniMax OpenAI-compatible `/v1/models` endpoint

entries.title: Close leaked file handle in orgnode parser
entries.body:
## Summary

`src/khoj/processor/content/org_mode/orgnode.py:57` opens a file with `open(filename, "r")` but never closes it. The file handle leaks for the lifetime of the returned `Orgnode` list.

## Fix

Replaced bare `open()` with a `with` statement to ensure the file is closed after `makelist()` finishes reading.

```python
# Before
def makelist_with_filepath(filename):
    f = open(filename, "r")
    return makelist(f, filename)

# After
def makelist_with_filepath(filename):
    with open(filename, "r") as f:
        return makelist(f, filename)
```

This is safe because `makelist()` fully consumes the file during the call (building the Orgnode list from file contents), so the file handle is no longer needed after it returns.

entries.title: Fix operator precedence in research iteration counter
entries.body:
## Summary

Fix a Python operator precedence bug in the `research()` function that causes `current_iteration` to be set to a boolean instead of the actual count of previous iterations.

## Bug

```python
if current_iteration := len(previous_iterations) > 0:
```

Python evaluates this as:
```python
if current_iteration := (len(previous_iterations) > 0):  # assigns True or False
```

So `current_iteration` becomes `True` (1) or `False` (0) regardless of how many previous iterations exist.

## Fix

```python
if (current_iteration := len(previous_iterations)) > 0:
```

With parentheses, `current_iteration` is correctly set to the count (e.g. 4), and then compared to 0.

## Impact

When resuming research with previous iterations, the loop counter was effectively reset to 1 instead of the true count. This allowed the research loop to run significantly more iterations than `MAX_ITERATIONS` intended, wasting compute and API calls.

entries.title: Fix extract_from_webpage discarding pre-fetched content
entries.body:
## Summary

In `extract_from_webpage()`, the `content` parameter is unconditionally overwritten to `None` on the line before the `is_none_or_empty(content)` check. This means any pre-fetched content (e.g. text content already retrieved by the Exa search engine) is always discarded, forcing an unnecessary re-scrape of the webpage.

## Bug

```python
async def extract_from_webpage(
    url: str,
    subqueries: set[str] = None,
    content: str = None,     # <-- caller passes pre-fetched content
    ...
) -> Tuple[set[str], str, Union[None, str]]:
    content = None            # <-- BUG: immediately overwrites it
    if is_none_or_empty(content):  # always True
        content = await scrape_webpage_with_fallback(url)
```

## Fix

Remove the `content = None` assignment so the passed-in content is used when available, falling back to scraping only when needed.

This bug was introduced in a refactor and causes:
- Wasted API calls to web scrapers for pages whose content is already available
- Increased latency for search results that include inline content (e.g. Exa)
